identity: A grade-school Arabic language-arts textbook page built around a children's rhymed chant (نشيد) titled النحات 'The Sculptor'. Three blocks in sequence. (1) The poem, printed one short verse line per <NL>, with the refrain قال سلام / يا تمام opening and closing the body, and a final stanza in the sculptor's own voice (الحجر الصامت إنسان … واسمي في فني النحات). Rhyme confirms the line grid: قلمُ/رسموا share روي م, الحجرُ/نقروا/حفروا share ر, نافر/غائر/مغاور share ر, وسم/وشم share م. (2) An unlabelled vocabulary-gloss strip (@69–@87) running as one <NL> line: six headword+definition rows keyed to words the poem actually used — غائر، نافر، مغاور، الوسم والوشم، النقش، الرقش (حمع at @75 is a scanno for جمع). (3) A one-line comprehension exercise (@89–@97) ending in a question. Genre mix: K (verse) for the body, J4 (workbook term+gloss table) for the strip, J2 (exercise question) for the tail.
law: Three laws, one per block. POEM: the line is the unit. The source already prints one hemistich — sometimes less — per <NL>, so the <NL> grid does nearly all the work; a 2-word rhyming line is not shredded into its bare nouns, and noun+adjective, و/أو + bare noun, speech-verb + quote, and verb + subordinate complement all stay whole. The one exception is a line carrying two genuinely independent finite predications. GLOSS STRIP: the row is the unit — a headword stays welded to its definition and boundaries fall only between rows (J4), which is deliberately the opposite of the H1 colon cut. EXERCISE: ordinary prose law resumes — و introducing a new subject with its own finite verb and object = CUT, clause-initial ف + question = CUT, and parallelism overrides the short-tail brake.
reasoning: SITE 1, @19 أصغينا (my only genuinely contested site, marked lo). This is the sole poem line holding two independent finite predications: أصغينا (1pl) then حدثنا الحجر, which introduces a new subject, asyndetically. To merge: it is one <NL> line, the stranded fragment is a single word, and reading the whole line as one hemistich rhyming in الحجرُ is metrically tidy. To cut, which I did: (a) open-contradiction-2's working discriminator fires cleanly — the second clause introduces a NEW subject rather than continuing to predicate about the first, which is my cut side; (b) A6/E1/L1 all cut asyndeton of exactly this shape; (c) the relation is cataphoric — أصغينا announces and 'حدثنا الحجر عمن نقروا عمن حفروا' is its content, i.e. the H1 colon pattern, my single most mechanical repeated miss; (d) the decisive scale argument — gold is FORCED by <NL> to split حدثنا الحجر from its own prepositional complements عمن نقروا and عمن حفروا, so this document's established granularity is already sub-clausal, and a 1-token unit is not anomalous where 2-token units are the norm; (e) my measured profile is ~7:1 toward missed cuts, and specifically in verse (doc_20dcf69f9905 @143/@159) gold cut two clauses sharing one line while I merged them. I also confirmed the annotator does cut inside <NL> lines here, since the exercise line must be cut (see site 5) — so 'never add a boundary the <NL> didn't give' is not this document's rule. Cut at @19, lo. Rejected sub-variant: a cut at @20 (أصغينا حدثنا ‖ الحجر) is impossible, الحجر is the subject of حدثنا. SITE 2, @8–@11 حجر إزميل أو قلم. Three siblings could read as an option list under I4, which would force a cut before each. Rejected: an explicit أو coordinates the series, they are bare nouns carrying no predication (§0 conjunct-weight test → no cut; I5 makes an internal و/أو bare-noun coordination), and the whole line is one hemistich closing the rhyme on قلمُ. One unit. SITE 3, @13–@17 عرفوا من نحتوا أو رسموا. من is a relative/interrogative complementiser governed by عرفوا — a tight subordinator that never opens a unit (§2, الذي row); أو رسموا is a 1-word coordinated verb inside that same complement. Not the H1 pattern, since no list follows. One unit. SITE 4, the gloss strip @69–@87 — the document's principal decision. Parsed as six rows: غائر | عميق مجوف ‖ نافر | بارز ‖ مغاور | حمع[=جمع] مغارة ‖ الوسم والوشم | الرسم على الجلد ‖ النقش | الرسم على الحجر ‖ الرقش | التزيين. Every headword is a word the poem itself used, which independently validates the parse and leaves no token unassigned. Two of my rules collide here: H1 says a headword that announces a definition ends its own unit, J4 says a term and its gloss are one table row and must not be split. J4 wins, and not narrowly — its evidence base is twelve of my own false cuts in doc_20dcf69f9905, a grade-school poem-plus-exercises page of precisely this kind, where gold kept الأكاسيد, نفايات and سموم welded to their definitions; and open-contradiction-1's discriminator agrees, since these are not free-standing answer targets but cells paired with a partner cell in the same row. So no cut between term and gloss, cuts between rows: @71 مجوف, @73 بارز, @76 مغارة, @81 الجلد, @85 الحجر (@87 التزيين is already forced by the following <NL>). Strongest confirmation is the pair الوسم والوشم | الرسم على الجلد and النقش | الرسم على الحجر — two rows of identical shape, making @81 near-certain, and by back-formation the shorter rows before them. The row-internal و in الوسم والوشم is bare-noun و: no cut. Also rejected: treating the whole strip as one unit, which would ignore J4's explicit 'cut between rows' and the fact that gold in doc_20dcf69f9905 cut between rows with no <NL> to assist. Also rejected: J1 word-drill granularity (one word per unit) — these are not same-type siblings in a matching drill, they are dependent term/definition pairs. SITE 5, the exercise @89–@97: الرسام يرسم لوحة والشاعر يكتب قصيدة فماذا يفعل النحات. Three units. @91 لوحة — the conjunct والشاعر يكتب قصيدة brings its own subject, its own finite verb and its own object; the conjunct-weight test at its cleanest, and A1/B3/C1 make و + new finite predication non-negotiable. @94 قصيدة — clause-initial ف (B1, near-absolute) plus a question, and E4/J2 both make a question its own unit even when connective-joined; the 0c budget is also spent, two clauses already stated. The 3-word length of each fragment does not trigger the 0b short-tail brake: 0b is for non-parallel, dependent-feeling fragments, and B2 states outright that parallelism defeats it. Controlling precedent is J2's gold from this same textbook genre — بم تشبه المعلمة الأم ‖ وبم يشبه المعلم الأب — four words each, both cut. SITE 6, the remaining poem lines, all left whole with their forced pre-<NL> boundaries: قال سلام is E3, quoted content stays with its speech verb; يا تمام is a vocative address, not a speaker label, so E5 does not apply; رسم نافر and شكل غائر are noun+adjective; في أهرامات ومغاور is و + bare noun; نقش وسم and رقش وشم are two-noun appositive pairs and two siblings sit below I4's three-or-four threshold for list detection; الحجر الصامت إنسان is one nominal predication (subject|predicate, no cut at @52); يجعله ينطق فنان is one predication with fronted verb and فنان as its subject; أنا أعطي الأحجار حياة is one predication (أنا is its topic, no cut at @59); واسمي في فني النحات is one nominal predication and النحات is its khabar, not a dangling H1 stem. FORMAT CHECK: all 20 pre-<NL> tokens and the final token @97 are carried as boundaries; no boundary sits on an <NL> token.
